designSystem.styleGuidelines:
## Brand & Style
This design system establishes a welcoming, precise engineering workspace tailored for operations, requesters, and setup owners. The atmosphere is defined by bright surfaces, high-clarity data presentation, and a calm, functional aesthetic that prioritizes operational efficiency over decorative flair. 

The visual style merges principles of **Corporate / Modern** design with utilitarian clarity:
- **Purposeful Color:** Restrained use of blue, orange, and green accents to guide user attention to statuses and primary actions without visual noise.
- **Data-First Layout:** Information density is carefully calibrated. Decorative charts, large welcome banners, and unrelated activity feeds are intentionally omitted to keep focus entirely on the work queue.
- **Ergonomic Precision:** Generous spacing around primary actions combined with strict typographic hierarchies ensure operational data is read effortlessly.

## Layout & Spacing
The layout system implements a structured **fluid grid** built on an 8px rhythm, prioritizing the work queue as the dominant canvas area.

- **Desktop Layout:** A 1280px canvas featuring a fixed 200–216px navigation sidebar, 24–32px main padding, and 24px major-section gaps. The three summary controls sit prominently above a full-width request table.
- **Mobile Layout:** A 390px canvas wrapping the desktop sidebar into an accessible slide-out drawer, replacing the horizontal table with vertical list items, and utilizing 16px horizontal gutters with zero horizontal overflow.

## Elevation & Depth
Depth is handled with extreme restraint, relying on low-contrast outlines and flat tonal layering rather than heavy drop shadows.

- **Surface Tiers:** Surfaces are distinguished using precise background color shifts (e.g., pure white cards on a cool canvas background) bounded by quiet outline borders (`#DCE5EB`).
- **Focus States:** Interactive elements utilize accessible blue focus rings and clear outline/check treatments to indicate selection without relying on disruptive elevation shifts.

## Components
Components are built for operational clarity, speed, and high information density.

- **Buttons:** Primary actions utilize solid accessible blue (`#006F95`) with white text, maintaining a 40–44px height and visible focus rings. Secondary controls feature clean outlines.
- **Navigation:** Compact NXP wordmark paired with clear icon-and-label pairs. Active states feature a blue wash (`#E8F6FC`) and a colored leading indicator.
- **Summary Controls:** Side-by-side interactive filter tiles (Open work, Overdue, Completed) featuring tinted surfaces and restrained icons. They act as real queue filters rather than decorative statistics.
- **Queue / Tables:** A dominant full-width surface featuring keyword search, Status selectors, and Clear filters. Rows contain request titles/numbers, current statuses, due dates, and owners, with urgent/high priority indicated via small readable badges.
- **Inputs & Cards:** Clean, bordered input fields paired with subtly padded panels (16–24px padding) that avoid unnecessary card nesting.

# PSF Request Portal — NXP-inspired redesign

## 1. Visual theme and atmosphere

Approved brief, 4 October 2026: design in Stitch only, one page at a time. Serve Requesters and Setup Owners, English interface, desktop with mobile layouts, light mode first. Reduce information displayed simultaneously and add purposeful color. Complete and review Dashboard before designing another route. Admin screens and dark mode are deferred.

Use a welcoming, precise engineering workspace: bright surfaces, clear hierarchy, restrained blue/orange/green accents, generous spacing around primary actions, and readable operational data. No decorative charts, large welcome banner, unrelated activity feed, or additional KPI tiles. Display work first.

Source baseline: React/TanStack Router, custom CSS, Inter and JetBrains Mono; current primary #245BBD, sidebar #14263E, background #EEF2F7. The imported Dashboard image is the recorded top-panel layout in output/playwright/top-panels/after/dashboard-desktop.png. Its DEMO requests and Development identities are documented test data, not production business records. This document specifies the proposed redesign, not an extraction claiming these proposed tokens already exist in the application.

## 2. Color palette and roles

These are NXP-inspired interface colors, not a claim of strict official CI compliance.

| Token | Color | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paper | #FFFFFF | Navigation, table, inputs |
| Cool canvas | #F4F7FA | Page background |
| Quiet outline | #DCE5EB | Dividers and panel borders |
| Ink | #173248 | Main text |
| Secondary ink | #526575 | Supporting text |
| NXP-inspired blue | #00A9E0 | Brand accents and open-work icon/background accent |
| Accessible action blue | #006F95 | Primary actions, links and focused controls with white text |
| Blue wash | #E8F6FC | Active navigation and open-work summary |
| NXP-inspired orange | #FCA600 | Warm accent and overdue-summary decoration |
| Orange ink | #8A4700 | Readable warning text |
| Orange wash | #FFF3DA | Overdue summary surface |
| NXP-inspired green | #69CA00 | Brand accent and completed-summary decoration |
| Green ink | #28651D | Readable success text |
| Green wash | #EDF8E5 | Completed summary surface |
| Error ink | #B42332 | Errors and overdue record labels |
| Error wash | #FFF0F1 | Error surfaces |

Use darker ink on bright accents; do not put small white text on bright orange, lime green, or cyan. Every status has a text label and icon. Selection uses an outline/check treatment as well as color. Distinguish Overdue from merely Urgent priority.

## 3. Typography rules

Inter for English UI. Use JetBrains Mono sparingly for request numbers, with tabular numerals for counts/dates.

| Style | Size / line height | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page title | 28 / 36 px | 600 |
| Section heading | 18 / 26 px | 600 |
| Summary count | 28 / 36 px | 600 |
| Body and controls | 14 / 22 px | 400–500 |
| Request title | 14 / 22 px | 600 |
| Supporting label | 12 / 18 px | 400–500 |

Use ordinary title/sentence case. Limit competing headings. Full custom status names must remain available when their compact display is truncated. Avoid tiny uppercase labels repeated in every row.

## 4. Component stylings

Buttons: 40–44 px desktop height, 44 px minimum touch area; solid accessible blue for the primary New Request action, simple outlined secondary controls, 8 px radius and visible focus state.

Navigation: approximately 200–216 px wide, light background, compact NXP wordmark/PSF identity, icon plus visible English label; active Dashboard uses blue wash and a colored leading indicator. Requester links: Dashboard, Requests, My Drafts, Export, History. Setup Owner omits Export and adds the existing department scope control inside Dashboard. Do not expose Admin tools to these roles. Do not invent a role-switching control.

Summary controls: exactly Open work, Overdue, Completed, side by side above the work queue, with blue/orange/green tinted surfaces and restrained icons. These are real queue filter controls in the proposed interaction, not decorative statistics. An empty completed count is valid.

Queue: one dominant full-width surface with a short heading, keyword search, Status selector and Clear filters. No secondary rail consuming table width. A row contains only request title/number, current status, due date and owner/department; urgent/high priority can be a small readable indicator near the date. Product type and extra metadata move into request detail. Show around five representative rows in the design, with the existing 25-item pagination contract retained and scroll available. Long titles and configurable status names need bounded wrapping plus access to their full value.

Use a restrained 8–12 px panel radius, fine borders, little or no shadow, 16–24 px panel padding. Do not place every value in a separate card.

## 5. Layout principles

Desktop design canvas 1280 px wide, with 24–32 px main padding and 24 px major-section gaps on an 8 px rhythm. Keep the three summaries above the table, preserving the current top-panel structure. Keep greeting/description to one short line; make the table the dominant area.

Mobile design canvas 390 px wide: hide desktop rail behind a menu; preserve labeled navigation in the drawer; compact top bar; three compact summary controls; persistent keyword search and a Filters button opening secondary filters; request rows become compact vertical list items rather than a horizontally overflowing table. Each item shows title/number, status, due date and owner with an accessible open action. Use 16 px horizontal gutters and no horizontal page overflow. Preserve role and scope rules.

## 6. Stitch generation notes and constraints

Current page only: /dashboard. Import the existing UI reference, then edit the uploaded screen. Do not generate or upload other routes until this page is reviewed.

Requester and Setup Owner share the same layout. Owner-specific scope values must remain exactly Related work, Created by me and PSF department work; do not replace this with Assigned to me because assignment is not the current query contract. Requester sees related work under their existing permissions. Treat owner scope as a documented responsive state of this Dashboard, not another route.

Keep the current workflow rules: statuses are admin-configurable and are not a mandatory linear sequence. No percent-complete chart, stepper, invented approvals, assignee write action, file generation, notifications count, or unsupported bulk action. No per-row export action for Owner. New Request opens the existing private-draft creation flow; do not imply it submits immediately. Only show explicitly fictional sample content in newly designed views.

Prompt direction: "Rework the imported Dashboard into a light NXP-inspired work queue with three compact, colored summary filter tiles above a calm full-width request list. Show the existing work controls clearly and place secondary information in the detail view. Keep all text in English and preserve Requester/Setup Owner permissions."

variants.prompt:
Generate EXACTLY 1 variant of this mobile dashboard (390px viewport) as the DARK COUNTERPART with a working LOCAL Light/Dark theme toggle for design preview.

Start in DARK MODE by default:
- data-theme="dark" on root/html/body.
- Dark canvas #101B24, navigation/drawer #14232F, surfaces/cards #1A2C39, outlines/borders #344A59, primary text #EDF4F8, secondary text #B3C4D0.
- NXP cyan #00A9E0, orange #FCA600, green #69CA00 accents. Small links #55C8EF.
- Summary washes: deep blue/brown/green with bright readable text and icons; avoid huge bright blocks.
  - Open work (selected): deep blue wash (e.g. rgba(0, 169, 224, 0.15)), border #00A9E0, count 44, badge "Filtered" with checkmark.
  - Overdue: deep orange/brown wash (e.g. rgba(252, 166, 0, 0.15)), border rgba(252, 166, 0, 0.35), count 24, "View ->".
  - Completed: deep green wash (e.g. rgba(105, 202, 0, 0.15)), border rgba(105, 202, 0, 0.35), count 6, "View ->".
- Primary New Request button: solid cyan/accessible blue with dark high-contrast text or high contrast styling, fully opaque, enabled, 44px min height.
- Theme toggle in the mobile top bar (min 44x44px touch target):
  - Accessible name and title: "Switch to light mode" when in dark mode, showing a Sun icon.
  - When clicked, a small vanilla JavaScript snippet toggles the theme between 'dark' and 'light' by changing `data-theme` on document.documentElement (or body), updating the button's aria-label and icon/text to "Switch to dark mode" (moon icon) in light mode, and vice-versa.
  - Shared CSS variables for both modes:
    - Light mode tokens: canvas #F4F7FA, paper/surfaces #FFFFFF, ink #173248, secondary ink #526575, borders #DCE5EB, blue wash #E8F6FC, orange wash #FFF3DA, green wash #EDF8E5, action #006F95 with white text.
    - Dark mode tokens: canvas #101B24, navigation #14232F, surfaces #1A2C39, outlines #344A59, text #EDF4F8, secondary text #B3C4D0, accents cyan #00A9E0, orange #FCA600, green #69CA00.
    - Theme toggling recolors every surface, card, input, text, border, and status badge without drifting DOM or layout.

Role & Permissions (Setup Owner · MFG):
- Role: Alex Morgan, Setup Owner · MFG. Avatar AM.
- Navigation drawer: Dashboard (active), Requests, My Drafts. NO Export, NO Admin, NO global History.
- Heading: "Dashboard", Subtitle: "Your related work, at a glance."
- Work scope: "PSF department work" is selected. Near the queue heading ("PSF department work"), show the explicit department pill/badge: "MFG Department" and "44 total".
- Work scope control inside the collapsed Filters disclosure has options: "Related work", "Created by me", "PSF department work" (selected).
- Status dropdown filter options must use exact catalog strings:
  - "All statuses" (selected)
  - "20% -- PSF File Creating"
  - "30% -- Compare Old and New layout"
  - "93% -- Provide test template map to EWFM\\Update auto FI script (ST Fab)"
  - "10% -- Test Engineer Data Entry"
  - "99% -- Wait requestor Buyoff site location and wafer map"
  - "100% -- Completed"
  - "0% -- Rejected (Cancel Request)"

Queue Rows (5 fictional illustrative rows):
- All 5 statuses shown are kind=open. Give all 5 consistent open-work blue/cyan styling (e.g. cyan outline/wash with text, no progress bar, no green success treatment even for 99%!).
- All 5 sample rows must have Owner / Dept as "MFG", never GNTC (e.g. Owner A / MFG, Owner B / MFG, Owner C / MFG, Owner A / MFG, Owner B / MFG).
- Rows:
  1. PSF wafer-map setup | SAMPLE-001 · PC-SAMPLE-A | 20% -- PSF File Creating | 01 Oct 2026 (! OVERDUE red badge, High priority) | Owner A / MFG
  2. Reference PSF layout comparison | SAMPLE-002 · PC-SAMPLE-B | 30% -- Compare Old and New layout | 07 Oct 2026 (Normal) | Owner B / MFG
  3. Template map and FI script update | SAMPLE-003 · PC-SAMPLE-C | 93% -- Provide test template map to EWFM\\Update auto FI script (ST Fab) | 09 Oct 2026 (Normal) | Owner C / MFG
  4. Probecard setup data entry | SAMPLE-004 · PC-SAMPLE-D | 10% -- Test Engineer Data Entry | 12 Oct 2026 (Urgent) | Owner A / MFG
  5. Wafer-map requester buyoff | SAMPLE-005 · PC-SAMPLE-E | 99% -- Wait requestor Buyoff site location and wafer map | 16 Oct 2026 (Low) | Owner B / MFG

Pagination Footer:
- Footer text: "Preview: 5 sample rows · 44 open requests · 25 per page"
- Pagination buttons: Previous disabled, "Page 1 of 2", Next enabled.

Layout & Accessibility:
- 390px mobile viewport, 16px horizontal gutters, zero horizontal overflow.
- Minimum 44px touch targets on buttons and interactive controls.
- Explicit accessible labels on search ("Search requests", placeholder "Request no., title, PSF or probecard"), filter buttons, and dialogs.
